items.title: In Praise of Kayak, 21 Years Later
items.summary: Nobody has built a better travel search tool than Kayak. There, I said it.

items.title: The New Long-Haul Routes Testing How Far Demand Really Stretches
items.summary: From Sapporo to Riyadh, airlines are getting bolder with their long-haul route bets and using efficient widebody jets to test markets that may once have seemed too niche.

items.title: Viator’s Updated Operator Agreement Formalizes a Power Shift in Experiences Pricing: Scoop
items.summary: Is Airbnb's partnership with Tripadvisor merely an expansion of Airbnb's partnership with Tripadvisor's res-tech unit Bokun? So far some Airbnb employees aren't seeing signs of a broad, new Viator inventory partnership in the works.

items.title: The Iran War Shows How Reliant Indian Airlines Are on Gulf Hubs
items.summary: India’s global aviation ambitions still run through the Gulf. When that works, it connects Indian travelers to the world. When geopolitics disrupts it, the shock quickly reaches India’s airlines.

items.title: Travel’s AI Reckoning Has Arrived
items.summary: Sarah Kopit and Seth Borko break down travel’s AI reckoning: what is paying off, what is still experimental, and why data, trust, and ROI now matter more than AI hype.

items.title: Hilton’s CEO on Why the Fundamentals Still Win in the AI Era
items.summary: As AI models increasingly decide who gets recommended, Chris Nassetta's view is that the inputs still hold. Reliability, culture, and a lifetime relationship with the guest keep earning the recommendation, even as who does the recommending has changed.

items.title: Expedia Cuts Eight Executives as It Reorganizes Around AI
items.summary: Expedia Group is shedding several senior leaders and shifting others around to reshape leadership and work structure. The goal: To help product and technology efforts move faster.
